hints: Focus on which functional groups can produce a carboxylate ion, $\text{RCOO}^-$, when treated with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$.
Notice that the top two structures are a methyl ester and a free carboxylic acid, and both contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C=O}$ unit.
Check the bottom two structures in the same way, one is a propyl ester of methanoic acid and the other is a branched carboxylic acid, then count how many give a sodium carboxylate.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two routes to a sodium carboxylate**

Think like this. A carboxylic acid gives a salt by simple neutralisation, and an ester gives a salt by alkaline hydrolysis.

$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{RCOOR'} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Classify the top two compounds**

Top left is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$, methyl propanoate, an ester. It hydrolyses to sodium propanoate and methanol.

Top right is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, propanoic acid, a carboxylic acid. It neutralises to sodium propanoate and water. So that is 2 so far.

**Classify the bottom two compounds**

Bottom left is $\text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, propyl methanoate, an ester. It hydrolyses to sodium methanoate and propan-1-ol.

Bottom right is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$, 2-methylpropanoic acid, a carboxylic acid. It neutralises to its sodium salt and water.

**Count and conclude**

All four structures, two acids and two esters, form $\text{RCOONa}$ with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. So the total is 4.

options.A: 1 is too low. It suggests only acids or only one ester reacts. In fact both carboxylic acids react by neutralisation and both esters react by alkaline hydrolysis to give a carboxylate salt.
options.B: 2 is too low. Students often count only the two carboxylic acids (top right and bottom right) and forget that esters also give sodium carboxylates on warming with aqueous NaOH.
options.C: 3 is one short. Students sometimes miss that the bottom left molecule is an ester, propyl methanoate $\text{HCOOR}$, because the $\text{H-C=O}$ end looks unusual, but it still hydrolyses to sodium methanoate.
options.D: 4 is correct. Top left and bottom left are esters that undergo alkaline hydrolysis, top right and bottom right are carboxylic acids that undergo neutralisation. All four produce $\text{RCOONa}$.
